To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Motec wrist joint prostheses can fail because of the ball and socket articulation and that adverse reactions to metal debris and polyether ether keton can develop.

2 patients with Motec wrist arthroplasties developed complications related to the articulation, one with a cobalt chromium adverse reaction to metal particles and one with a polyether ether ketonewear related problem.

the Motec wrist prosthesis is associated with an increased risk of adverse reactions to metal debris and wear related polyether ether ketonosis, both of which can lead to implant loosening and failure.

the development of a novel and innovative implant design for total wrist arthrodesis.
the design of a new generation of total wrist arthro-plasties.
the development of a new generation of implantable devices, which will provide a more reliable and longer lasting solution to the problems associated with current implant designs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Motec wrist joint prosthesis is not the best option at the present time.
a Motec prosthesis is not recommended for total wrist arthrodesis.
polyether ether ketones are not a suitable material for articulation in total joint prostheses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Motec wrist joint prosthesis should be avoided in young patients and patients with high activity level, as the polyether ether keton cup may wear and lead to adverse reactions.
the Motec wrist joint prosthesis should be removed when there is evidence of adverse reactions to either the metal or the plastic articulation.
the Motec wrist prosthesis should be removed when there is evidence of a pseudotumour, or a cystic lesion with black fluid and a black lining.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Motec wrist joint prostheses have a high failure rate due to a lack of durability of the articulating surfaces.
the Motec wrist joint is a high risk implant and should be used with extreme caution.
Motec total wrist joint arthroplasty is associated with a risk of adverse reactions to metal debris and adverse reactions to polyether etherketone.
